newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran oil official cautious over 1997 oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil official cautious over 1997 oil prices.

text.p: Hojattolah Ghanimifard, head of international affairs at National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), was reported on Thursday as expressing caution over the durability of current strong oil prices into 1997.
"The situation in the market shows that one should not be optimistic about having the same level of prices next year," Ghanimifard told the Iran daily newspaper.

He highlighted higher oil production from non-OPEC states, the possible return of Iraq to world markets and a failure by consumers to build up strategic stocks as factors that could put downward pressure on prices next year.

Ghanimifard, who has charge over Iran's 2.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude exports, referred to unnamed analysts' forecasts that North Sea Brent crude would average between $17 and $21 a barrel next year.
Dated Brent was trading at $24.10-15 a barrel on Thursday.
